description: Dhubri Pilot — WhatsApp/SMS/IVR chat simulation scenarios. Each scenario is a scripted sequence of 'beats' (timed message events) across simulated phone windows for each actor, plus a live case/dashboard panel. This drives simulator.html — a standalone, no-backend demo of how the coordination flow plays out, per CONCEPT.md/SOP.md/FLOWS.md. Nothing here talks to a real Glific/Gupshup/Exotel/Supabase account; it's a scripted walkthrough for demonstrating the design to someone before the full build.

beatSchema.at: milliseconds offset from scenario start, used for demo pacing (compressed vs. real elapsed time)
beatSchema.actor: which window this beat renders into — an actor id from this scenario's actors[], or 'dashboard'
beatSchema.from: 'bot' (automated system message to that actor) | an actor id (that persona's own outgoing message) | 'system' (dashboard/note entries)
beatSchema.kind: text | buttons | list | voice | photo | location | case_update | note
beatSchema.body: message text, or the note/case_update annotation
beatSchema.status: for kind=case_update — the case's new status
beatSchema.caseId: for kind=case_update — which case (optional, defaults to the scenario's running case)

scenarios.title: Happy path — worker-reported night emergency
scenarios.summary: The primary flow (SOP-1): a frontline worker reports directly, no verification gate needed. Shows the core fix this system exists for — boat dispatch and facility alert firing in parallel, not sequentially — plus pool broadcast with first-accept-wins.

scenarios.title: Family report — worker confirms, proceeds normally
scenarios.summary: SOP-2's main path: an unregistered family member raises a case on the public line, but it stays pending-verification until the char's frontline worker confirms — only then does boat/facility dispatch fire.

scenarios.title: Family report — worker unreachable, timeout auto-escalates
scenarios.summary: SOP-2 step 5's harder case: nobody confirms the family report in time. The pilot-default tradeoff errs toward dispatching anyway rather than risking a delayed real emergency — but flags the case for control-room review either way.

scenarios.title: Boatman pool doesn't respond — escalates to 108/CNES
scenarios.summary: SOP-3 step 4: nobody in the private boatman pool accepts within the escalation window, so the case automatically escalates to the 108/CNES ambulance channel and gets flagged for control-room attention.

scenarios.title: Omnichannel — SMS and IVR boatmen, no WhatsApp needed
scenarios.summary: CONCEPT.md §6a in action: the pool for this char has a WhatsApp boatman, an SMS-only boatman, and an IVR/feature-phone boatman. All three get the same broadcast simultaneously over their own channel; the IVR boatman accepts by pressing a digit on a live call — none of this touches Glific for the non-WhatsApp contacts.
